boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain San Francisco State University
boards.description: Verified late-hour food and activity stops on campus and in the immediately surrounding Stonestown, Lakeside, and Westlake area.

cards.title: Open24
cards.subtitle: Between J. Paul Leonard Library and the Administration Building
cards.notes: Use the on-campus vending stop when staffed vendors are closed; it is positioned between the library and Administration Building for anytime snacks and drinks.
cards.short_summary: A campus vending stop with round-the-clock access during fall and spring semesters.
cards.evidence_claim: SF State University Corporation identifies Open24 as open 24 hours a day, seven days a week during fall and spring semesters.
cards.source_title: Convenience Stores | The University Corporation, SF State
cards.access_notes: Fall and spring semester hours are listed as 24 hours a day, 7 days a week; the page currently notes it is under maintenance.

cards.title: Papa Johns Pizza Cambon Drive
cards.subtitle: 69 Cambon Drive, San Francisco
cards.notes: Choose carryout or delivery from the Cambon Drive shop when you need a later food option near the southwest edge of campus.
cards.short_summary: A pizza carryout and delivery location with hours extending into the early morning.
cards.evidence_claim: Papa Johns lists carryout and delivery at 69 Cambon Drive until 2 AM Monday through Wednesday and until 3 AM Thursday through Sunday.
cards.source_title: Papa Johns Cambon Drive | Papa Johns San Francisco, CA
cards.access_notes: Carryout and delivery are listed until 2 AM Monday–Wednesday and 3 AM Thursday–Sunday.

cards.title: Shake Shack Stonestown Galleria
cards.subtitle: 3251 20th Ave., San Francisco
cards.notes: Head to the Stonestown storefront for a late food stop with dine-in, pickup, and delivery options listed by the restaurant.
cards.short_summary: A Stonestown food stop open through midnight or 1 AM, depending on the day.
cards.evidence_claim: Shake Shack lists its Stonestown Galleria location open until midnight Sunday through Wednesday and until 1 AM Thursday through Saturday.
cards.source_title: Shake Shack at 3251 20th Ave. San Francisco, CA
cards.access_notes: Store hours are 10 AM–midnight Sunday–Wednesday and 10 AM–1 AM Thursday–Saturday.

cards.entity_name: Round1 Bowling and Arcade Stonestown Galleria
cards.title: Round1 Bowling and Arcade
cards.subtitle: 285 Winston Dr., Stonestown Galleria
cards.notes: Plan an evening of bowling, arcade games, billiards, or karaoke at this Stonestown venue; check activity availability and fees before arriving.
cards.short_summary: A late-open Stonestown entertainment venue with bowling and arcade activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Round1 lists its Stonestown Galleria location at 285 Winston Drive as open daily from 10 AM to 2 AM.
cards.source_title: Round1 Bowling and Arcade | Stonestown Galleria
cards.access_notes: Hours of operation are listed as daily, 10 AM–2 AM. Individual activities may have separate availability and charges.

cards.title: Marugame Udon
cards.subtitle: 3251 20th Ave., Stonestown Galleria
cards.notes: Use the Stonestown location for a sit-down or takeout noodle stop later than most campus vendors, and confirm service before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A Stonestown udon restaurant listed open nightly until 10 PM.
cards.evidence_claim: Marugame Udon lists its San Francisco Stonestown Galleria location as open daily from 10:30 AM to 10 PM.
cards.source_title: San Francisco ~ Stonestown Galleria | Marugame Udon
cards.access_notes: Daily hours are listed as 10:30 AM–10 PM.

cards.title: Original Joe's Westlake
cards.subtitle: 11 Glenwood Ave., Daly City
cards.notes: Reserve or check in with the Westlake restaurant for a later seated meal; regular menu service is listed through the evening every day.
cards.short_summary: A Westlake restaurant with nightly service to 10 PM and later Friday and Saturday closing.
cards.evidence_claim: Original Joe's lists Westlake hours until 10 PM Sunday through Thursday and until 11 PM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Westlake — Original Joe's
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are 11 AM–10 PM Monday–Thursday and Sunday, and until 11 PM Friday and Saturday.

cards.entity_name: Subway at Village at Centennial Square
cards.title: Subway at Village at Centennial Square
cards.subtitle: Village at Centennial Square, SF State
cards.notes: Keep this campus Village counter in mind for an evening sandwich before it closes; its published schedule includes both weekday and weekend service.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus sandwich counter with evening hours every day of the week.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Corporation lists Subway at Village at Centennial Square open until 8 PM weekdays and until 7 PM on weekends.
cards.source_title: Food Vendors | The University Corporation, SF State
cards.access_notes: Hours are listed as 9 AM–8 PM Monday–Friday and 10 AM–7 PM Saturday–Sunday.

cards.title: Tang Bar Stonestown
cards.subtitle: 3251 20th Ave., second floor, Stonestown Galleria
cards.notes: Check the Stonestown hot-pot restaurant for a Friday or Saturday evening meal; its official contact page separates dine-in, pickup, and delivery hours.
cards.short_summary: A Stonestown restaurant with Friday and Saturday dining hours through 9 PM.
cards.evidence_claim: Tang Bar lists Stonestown dining hours until 9 PM on Friday and Saturday, with earlier closing on other days.
cards.source_title: Contact Tang Bar San Francisco Stonestown
cards.access_notes: Dining hours are listed until 9 PM Friday–Saturday; pickup and delivery close earlier.

cards.title: Blondie's Pizza Stonestown
cards.subtitle: 3251 20th Ave., Stonestown Galleria
cards.notes: Use the Stonestown counter for a pizza option on Friday or Saturday evenings; check the store schedule because weekday and Sunday closing times are earlier.
cards.short_summary: A Stonestown pizza counter open until 9 PM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Blondie's Pizza lists its Stonestown location open until 9 PM Friday and Saturday, until 8 PM Monday through Thursday, and until 7 PM Sunday.
cards.source_title: Blondie's Pizza
cards.access_notes: Stonestown hours are listed as 11 AM–9 PM Friday–Saturday; weekday and Sunday hours end earlier.

cards.title: Le Soleil Stonestown
cards.subtitle: 3251 20th Ave., Suite 221, Stonestown Galleria
cards.notes: Consider this Stonestown dining room for a Friday or Saturday meal before the later mall-area counters close; reservations are available from its official page.
cards.short_summary: A Stonestown restaurant with Friday and Saturday hours through 8:30 PM.
cards.evidence_claim: Le Soleil lists Stonestown Galleria hours until 8:30 PM on Friday and Saturday, with 8 PM closing Monday through Thursday.
cards.source_title: Reserve a Table at Le Soleil Stonestown
cards.access_notes: Hours are listed until 8:30 PM Friday–Saturday; Monday–Thursday end at 8 PM and Sunday at 7 PM.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named campus spaces for focused work, collaborative projects, making, art, and reflection.

cards.title: Collaboration Studio
cards.subtitle: J. Paul Leonard Library, LIB 124
cards.notes: Bring a project group to the first-floor studio, use its computers or printers, and reserve a study room when you need a contained work session.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor library workspace built for collaborative study and practical tech tasks.
cards.evidence_claim: The Collaboration Studio has computers, printers, reservable study rooms, a peer-mentor help desk, and large tables for collaborative work.
cards.source_title: Centering students’ needs in reimagined spaces
cards.access_notes: Located on the first floor of J. Paul Leonard Library; study rooms are reservable.

cards.title: The Living Room
cards.subtitle: J. Paul Leonard Library, LIB 124C
cards.notes: Take a deliberate break between classes with a puzzle, craft, or leisure book, then return to the adjacent Collaboration Studio when it is time to work.
cards.short_summary: A daylight-filled library room set up for restorative breaks as well as quiet downtime.
cards.evidence_claim: The Living Room is attached to the Collaboration Studio and offers natural light, armchairs, puzzles, crafts, and leisure-reading books.
cards.source_title: Centering students’ needs in reimagined spaces
cards.access_notes: Located in LIB 124C, attached to the first-floor Collaboration Studio.

cards.title: Silent Study Room
cards.subtitle: J. Paul Leonard Library, LIB 41
cards.notes: Choose this ground-floor room for distraction-light reading or writing; plan to keep conversation, food, phones, and audio outside the room.
cards.short_summary: A designated silent library room for heads-down individual work.
cards.evidence_claim: The Silent Study Room is on the library ground floor, and talking, eating, phone use, and audio devices are not allowed there.
cards.source_title: Centering students’ needs in reimagined spaces
cards.access_notes: Ground floor; the library floor map identifies it as LIB 41.

cards.title: Digital Media Studio and MakerSpace
cards.subtitle: J. Paul Leonard Library, LIB 260
cards.notes: Use this second-floor studio when a class project needs 3D printing, VR, high-end computers, specialized software, scanning, or equipment checkout.
cards.short_summary: A hands-on media-production space with digital tools and equipment support.
cards.evidence_claim: The Digital Media Studio and MakerSpace supports SFSU projects with 3D printers, VR headsets, high-end computers, specialized software, scanning, and equipment checkout.
cards.source_title: Digital Media Studio and MakerSpace
cards.access_notes: LIB 260 on the library’s second floor; the official page lists regular-semester hours.

cards.title: Special Collections & Archives Gallery
cards.subtitle: J. Paul Leonard Library, LIB 462
cards.notes: Stop by the fourth-floor gallery to spend time with the current exhibition, then check the library events page for related talks or gallery programs.
cards.short_summary: A fourth-floor exhibition gallery next to Special Collections & Archives.
cards.evidence_claim: The Special Collections Gallery is on the fourth floor beside the Special Collections & Archives Reading Room, and exhibitions are free and open to the campus community and public.
cards.source_title: Spaces | J. Paul Leonard Library
cards.access_notes: Fourth floor, adjacent to the Special Collections & Archives Reading Room.

cards.title: Special Collections & Archives Reading Room
cards.subtitle: J. Paul Leonard Library, LIB 460
cards.notes: Plan an archival-research visit when your topic calls for rare books or primary sources; contact Special Collections first if you need help preparing a request.
cards.short_summary: A fourth-floor reading room for working with rare books and primary-source material.
cards.evidence_claim: SFSU directs students seeking rare books and primary-source material to the Special Collections & Archives Reading Room on the library’s fourth floor.
cards.source_title: Information for Students | J. Paul Leonard Library
cards.access_notes: Fourth-floor LIB 460; contact Special Collections & Archives for research assistance or access questions.

cards.title: Quiet Study
cards.subtitle: J. Paul Leonard Library, LIB 485
cards.notes: Head to the fourth floor when you need a calmer reading or drafting block, and keep voices low so the shared quiet-study setting remains usable.
cards.short_summary: A designated fourth-floor quiet-study area among the library’s open stacks.
cards.evidence_claim: The library’s fourth floor is a quiet study area, and its floor map identifies Quiet Study in LIB 485.
cards.source_title: Floor Maps | J. Paul Leonard Library
cards.access_notes: Fourth floor; designated quiet areas require low voices and minimal talking.

cards.title: Garden of Remembrance
cards.subtitle: Between Burk Hall and the Fine Arts Building
cards.notes: Use the garden as a reflective pause on the way across campus, and read its memorial elements with attention to the history they commemorate.
cards.short_summary: A campus memorial garden honoring Japanese American incarceration and affected SF State students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Garden of Remembrance honors Japanese Americans incarcerated during World War II, including 19 SF State students, and is free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Visit the Garden | Fine Arts Gallery
cards.access_notes: Located between Burk Hall and the Fine Arts Building; east and west entrances are described by the gallery.

cards.title: Associated Students Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: Cesar Chavez Student Center, T-139
cards.notes: Check the exhibition schedule before visiting, then use a current show or reception as a starting point for conversation about artists and community issues.
cards.short_summary: A student-funded, student-staffed gallery presenting visual and interdisciplinary work.
cards.evidence_claim: Associated Students describes its Art Gallery as student-funded and student-staffed; it presents student, faculty, and professional work and hosts exhibits and events.
cards.source_title: Art Gallery | Associated Students
cards.access_notes: Located in the Student Center at T-139; consult the gallery’s current exhibition information before visiting.

cards.title: Events Room
cards.subtitle: J. Paul Leonard Library, LIB 121
cards.notes: Look at the library events calendar before crossing the quad; use a listed workshop, talk, or program as an easy way to connect coursework with campus life.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor library venue used for campus workshops, talks, and other programs.
cards.evidence_claim: The library identifies the Events Room as LIB 121 on the first floor and lists it as a frequent location for events and meetings.
cards.source_title: Spaces | J. Paul Leonard Library
cards.access_notes: LIB 121 on the first floor; availability changes when it is scheduled for events or meetings.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-admission ways to spend time on campus and around San Francisco, with access conditions noted.

cards.title: Browse the Global Museum
cards.subtitle: Fine Arts Building, Room 203
cards.notes: Meet in the Fine Arts Building to view the teaching museum’s cultural-heritage exhibitions; check academic-year hours before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A free campus museum visit with exhibits shaped by Museum Studies students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Global Museum states that admission is free and lists academic-year hours Tuesday through Thursday, 11 a.m. to 4 p.m.
cards.source_title: Global Museum | SF State Museum Studies
cards.access_notes: Fine Arts Building, Room 203; academic-year hours are Tuesday–Thursday, 11 a.m.–4 p.m., plus appointments.

cards.title: Walk the Garden of Remembrance
cards.subtitle: Between Burk Hall and the Fine Arts Building
cards.notes: Use either garden entrance for a quiet outdoor reset, then continue through the surrounding Fine Arts and Student Center area.
cards.short_summary: A campus garden with two documented entrances beside major student buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: SF State’s Fine Arts Gallery says the Garden of Remembrance is free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Visit the Garden | Fine Arts Gallery
cards.access_notes: East entrance is behind César Chávez Student Center; west entrance is to the right of Cafe Rosso.

cards.title: Catch a Depot event
cards.subtitle: César Chávez Student Center, Lower Conference Level
cards.notes: Check the venue’s calendar, then bring friends for an all-ages live-music, open-mic, art-social, or comedy-night program.
cards.short_summary: A student-run campus venue for free public events unless an event says otherwise.
cards.evidence_claim: Associated Students says Depot events are all ages and free and open to the public unless otherwise noted.
cards.source_title: The Depot | Associated Students
cards.access_notes: Most events take place Monday–Thursday between 6 and 9 p.m.; confirm the individual event listing.

cards.title: Read and regroup at the Library
cards.subtitle: 1630 Holloway Avenue, SF State campus
cards.notes: Choose collaborative floors for conversation or a quiet floor for reading, then browse books and periodicals available on open shelving.
cards.short_summary: A campus library open to the public, with distinct quiet and collaborative areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The library says it is open to the general public and that visitors may read materials on its third- and fourth-floor open shelves.
cards.source_title: Visiting J. Paul Leonard Library
cards.access_notes: Visitors can use open-shelf materials on site; borrowing requires eligibility or a paid community-borrower membership.

cards.title: Explore the Randall Museum
cards.subtitle: 199 Museum Way, San Francisco
cards.notes: Build a low-key outing around the museum’s science, nature, and arts exhibits; bring a friend and leave time for the hilltop setting.
cards.short_summary: A city museum with free admission and hands-on science, nature, and arts exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: Randall Museum lists admission as free and regular hours Tuesday through Saturday, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.
cards.source_title: Hours and Directions | Randall Museum
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Saturday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; closed Sunday and Monday, plus listed holidays.

cards.title: Take an Ocean Beach walk
cards.subtitle: Golden Gate National Recreation Area, western San Francisco
cards.notes: Walk the shoreline, watch seabirds, or fly a kite; stay out of hazardous surf and pack out anything you bring.
cards.short_summary: A no-admission beach walk with wide-open shoreline and National Park Service guidance.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service identifies Ocean Beach as part of Golden Gate National Recreation Area, which is fee-free year-round with no entrance fee or pass required.
cards.source_title: Ocean Beach | Golden Gate National Recreation Area
cards.access_notes: The NPS recommends strolling and kite flying; swimming and wading can be hazardous because of strong currents.

cards.title: Walk Fort Funston’s bluffs
cards.subtitle: Golden Gate National Recreation Area, southwest San Francisco
cards.notes: Take the Sunset Trail toward Battery Davis and pause for dune, cliff, and coastal views; respect posted habitat closures.
cards.short_summary: A fee-free National Park Service bluff walk with a named accessible trail.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service lists the Fort Funston wildflower walk with no activity fee; Golden Gate National Recreation Area is fee-free year-round.
cards.source_title: Wildflower Walk at Fort Funston | National Park Service
cards.access_notes: The Sunset Trail provides an accessible route toward Battery Davis; use marked trails and observe restrictions in habitat-protection areas.

cards.title: Use Museums For All at Asian Art
cards.subtitle: 200 Larkin Street, Civic Center
cards.notes: Eligible San Francisco residents can bring required benefit and residency proof for free walk-up admission; confirm gallery hours before traveling.
cards.short_summary: A cultural outing available free to qualifying San Francisco residents through Museums For All.
cards.evidence_claim: San Francisco Human Services Agency lists Asian Art Museum admission as free for Museums For All participants, with walk-up admission and no advance ticket.
cards.source_title: San Francisco Museums For All | SFHSA
cards.access_notes: Free admission requires an EBT or Medi-Cal card plus proof of San Francisco residence; special exhibits may need separate reservations.

cards.title: See comics at Cartoon Art Museum
cards.subtitle: 781 Beach Street, Fisherman’s Wharf
cards.notes: Eligible San Francisco residents can use the city access program for a no-admission comics outing; check current hours before leaving campus.
cards.short_summary: A free-access museum option for qualifying residents who want a comics-focused hang.
cards.evidence_claim: San Francisco Human Services Agency lists Cartoon Art Museum admission as free for Museums For All participants, with walk-up admission and no advance ticket.
cards.source_title: San Francisco Museums For All | SFHSA
cards.access_notes: Free admission requires an EBT or Medi-Cal card plus proof of San Francisco residence; the agency lists daily hours except Wednesday.

cards.title: Visit the de Young through Museums For All
cards.subtitle: 50 Hagiwara Tea Garden Drive, Golden Gate Park
cards.notes: If eligible, use the city program for a free art-museum visit, then make a plan around the listed Thursday-through-Sunday hours.
cards.short_summary: A Golden Gate Park art museum accessible without admission for qualifying residents.
cards.evidence_claim: San Francisco Human Services Agency lists de Young Museum admission as free for Museums For All participants, with walk-up admission and no advance ticket.
cards.source_title: San Francisco Museums For All | SFHSA
cards.access_notes: Free admission requires an EBT or Medi-Cal card plus proof of San Francisco residence; special exhibits may require separate reservations.

warnings: Museums For All cards require EBT or Medi-Cal and proof of San Francisco residence; verify individual museum hours and special-exhibit rules before travel.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten named study environments in J. Paul Leonard Library, with documented quiet, collaborative, reservable, computer, or wellness-oriented features.

cards.title: Quiet Study
cards.subtitle: Ground floor, J. Paul Leonard Library
cards.notes: Set up in the ground-floor quiet area when you need computers, printing, or scanning close to a designated low-noise study environment.
cards.short_summary: A quiet ground-floor work area with computers and printing.
cards.evidence_claim: The Library identifies LIB 42 as a Quiet Study space with Mac and PC desktop computers and scanners.
cards.source_title: Floor Maps | J. Paul Leonard Library
cards.access_notes: Library use requires an SFSU OneCard or SFSU ID; computer sign-in uses SFSU single sign-on, and printing requires a OneCard or mobile ID.

cards.title: Silent Study Room
cards.subtitle: Ground floor, J. Paul Leonard Library
cards.notes: Choose this ground-floor room for focused reading or writing; the Library describes it as a large silent room with windows.
cards.short_summary: A windowed silent-study room beside the ground-floor quiet area.
cards.evidence_claim: The Library's floor map labels LIB 41 as the Silent Study Room, and its Quiet Study page describes a large Silent Study Room with windows.
cards.source_title: Quiet Study | J. Paul Leonard Library
cards.access_notes: Located in the Library's ground-floor Quiet Study area; Library use requires an SFSU OneCard or SFSU ID.

cards.title: Ground-Floor Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Quiet Study area, ground floor
cards.notes: Reserve a LIB 40 room for solo or group work, then use the whiteboard wall and leave the room ready for the next reservation.
cards.short_summary: Twelve reservable rooms in the ground-floor quiet area.
cards.evidence_claim: The Library has 12 reservable study rooms on the ground floor in a quiet area; rooms may be used by one or more people.
cards.source_title: Reserve a Room | J. Paul Leonard Library
cards.access_notes: For SFSU students, faculty, and staff only. Reserve up to three hours daily, up to three days ahead; unoccupied rooms may be used until a reservation holder arrives.

cards.title: Collaboration Studio
cards.subtitle: First floor, J. Paul Leonard Library
cards.notes: Bring a project group to this first-floor collaborative area, where computers, printing, color scanning, a help desk, and study rooms are available.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor collaborative study area with technology and support.
cards.evidence_claim: The Collaboration Studio is a large first-floor collaborative study area with printing, color scanning, a help desk, study rooms, and Windows and Mac computers.
cards.source_title: Collaboration Studio | J. Paul Leonard Library
cards.access_notes: Computers use SFSU single sign-on; printing requires an SFSU OneCard or mobile ID. Library use requires an SFSU OneCard or SFSU ID.

cards.title: The Living Room
cards.subtitle: Attached to the Collaboration Studio, first floor
cards.notes: Use the armchairs and natural light for a low-key reading or planning session; puzzles, crafts, and leisure books support a study break.
cards.short_summary: A wellness-oriented room with armchairs, natural light, and leisure activities.
cards.evidence_claim: The Library describes The Living Room as a room attached to the Collaboration Studio with natural light, comfy armchairs, puzzles, crafts, and leisure-reading books.
cards.source_title: Centering students’ needs in reimagined spaces | J. Paul Leonard Library
cards.access_notes: The floor map places The Living Room in LIB 124 C, attached to the first-floor Collaboration Studio. Library use requires an SFSU OneCard or SFSU ID.

cards.title: First-Floor Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Collaboration Studio, first floor
cards.notes: Book one of these Collaboration Studio rooms when your group needs a defined workspace near computers, printing, scanning, and library help.
cards.short_summary: Six reservable rooms inside the first-floor Collaboration Studio.
cards.evidence_claim: The Library reports six reservable study rooms in the first-floor Collaboration Studio.
cards.source_title: Reserve a Room | J. Paul Leonard Library
cards.access_notes: For SFSU students, faculty, and staff only. Reserve up to three hours daily, up to three days ahead; unoccupied rooms may be used until a reservation holder arrives.

cards.title: Team Collaboration Spaces
cards.subtitle: Second floor, J. Paul Leonard Library
cards.notes: Plan a team session in one of the two second-floor collaboration spaces, positioned beside the open study area and group-study resources.
cards.short_summary: Two team-oriented rooms next to second-floor open study space.
cards.evidence_claim: The floor map lists Team Collaboration Space 1 and 2 on the second floor, alongside a study area and group study and media viewing.
cards.source_title: Floor Maps | J. Paul Leonard Library
cards.access_notes: The Library's reservation page identifies two Team Collaboration Spaces on the second floor in an open study area. Library use requires an SFSU OneCard or SFSU ID.

cards.title: Second-Floor Study Area
cards.subtitle: LIB 287, J. Paul Leonard Library
cards.notes: Use this second-floor open study area when you want to work near the Team Collaboration Spaces and the Library’s group-study and media-viewing area.
cards.short_summary: An open second-floor study area near team-work rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: The Library's second-floor map lists Study Area (LIB 287), Team Collaboration Space 1 and 2, and Group Study and Media Viewing.
cards.source_title: Floor Maps | J. Paul Leonard Library
cards.access_notes: Located on the Library's second floor. The Library describes its first through third floors as collaborative spaces; Library use requires an SFSU OneCard or SFSU ID.

cards.title: Third-Floor Study Area
cards.subtitle: LIB 360, J. Paul Leonard Library
cards.notes: Work among children’s books, government reference books, maps and atlases, microfiche, and microfilm when those collections support your assignment.
cards.short_summary: A third-floor study area alongside reference collections and maps.
cards.evidence_claim: The Library's third-floor map lists Study Area (LIB 360) with children's books, government reference books, maps and atlases, microfiche, and microfilm.
cards.source_title: Floor Maps | J. Paul Leonard Library
cards.access_notes: Located on the Library's third floor, which the Library describes as a collaborative space. Library use requires an SFSU OneCard or SFSU ID.

cards.title: Fourth-Floor Quiet Study
cards.subtitle: LIB 485, J. Paul Leonard Library
cards.notes: Head to the fourth floor for a more peaceful study setting near books A–L and the Library’s theses and dissertations collection.
cards.short_summary: A fourth-floor quiet-study area near books and SFSU theses.
cards.evidence_claim: The Library's fourth-floor map labels LIB 485 as Quiet Study and SFSU Theses & Dissertations; it states that the fourth floor is a quiet study area.
cards.source_title: Floor Maps | J. Paul Leonard Library
cards.access_notes: Keep voices low and talking to a minimum in designated quiet-study areas. Library use requires an SFSU OneCard or SFSU ID.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on the 19th Avenue, Winston Drive, and 20th Avenue corridor immediately north of San Francisco State University.

cards.title: Stonestown Galleria
cards.subtitle: 20th Avenue corridor, north of SFSU
cards.notes: Use the mall directory to orient yourself to the corridor’s stores, food options, services, and indoor destinations before heading in.
cards.short_summary: A mapped retail and dining hub at 3251 20th Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: Stonestown Galleria’s official directory lists its address as 3251 20th Ave and identifies stores and restaurants on site.
cards.source_title: Stonestown Galleria Directory
cards.access_notes: Located on the 20th Avenue corridor, immediately north of campus.

cards.title: Whole Foods Market
cards.subtitle: 20th Avenue corridor at Stonestown Galleria
cards.notes: Check the official mall directory for this grocery stop’s placement, then plan any food or household-item pickup around your route.
cards.short_summary: A grocery destination listed in the Stonestown Galleria directory.
cards.evidence_claim: The Stonestown Galleria directory lists Whole Foods Market on Level 1 near Whole Foods.
cards.source_title: Stonestown Galleria Directory
cards.access_notes: On the 20th Avenue corridor within Stonestown Galleria.

cards.title: Trader Joe's
cards.subtitle: 20th Avenue corridor at Stonestown Galleria
cards.notes: Use the directory listing to locate this grocery stop near Target, then combine it with other errands in the same complex.
cards.short_summary: A grocery-store listing near Target at Stonestown.
cards.evidence_claim: The Stonestown Galleria directory lists Trader Joe’s on Level 1 near Target.
cards.source_title: Stonestown Galleria Directory
cards.access_notes: On the 20th Avenue corridor within Stonestown Galleria.

cards.title: Target
cards.subtitle: 20th Avenue corridor at Stonestown Galleria
cards.notes: Use the mall directory’s Level 1 listing to make this a practical stop for everyday goods while already on the corridor.
cards.short_summary: A Level 1 Target listed in the Stonestown directory.
cards.evidence_claim: The Stonestown Galleria directory lists Target on Level 1 near Target.
cards.source_title: Stonestown Galleria Directory
cards.access_notes: On the 20th Avenue corridor within Stonestown Galleria.

cards.title: Regal Cinemas
cards.subtitle: 20th Avenue corridor at Stonestown Galleria
cards.notes: Consult current showtimes before traveling; the mall directory places this cinema on Level 2 within the Stonestown complex.
cards.short_summary: A Level 2 cinema destination in the mall corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The Stonestown Galleria directory lists Regal Cinemas on Level 2 near Regal Cinemas.
cards.source_title: Stonestown Galleria Directory
cards.access_notes: On the 20th Avenue corridor within Stonestown Galleria; tickets are required for screenings.

cards.title: Round1 Bowling & Arcade
cards.subtitle: 20th Avenue corridor at Stonestown Galleria
cards.notes: Find this Level 1 activity venue in the official directory and check the operator’s current offerings before planning a group visit.
cards.short_summary: A bowling-and-arcade venue listed at Stonestown.
cards.evidence_claim: The Stonestown Galleria directory lists Round1 Bowling & Arcade on Level 1.
cards.source_title: Stonestown Galleria Directory
cards.access_notes: On the 20th Avenue corridor within Stonestown Galleria; paid activities may apply.

cards.title: YMCA
cards.subtitle: 20th Avenue corridor at Stonestown Galleria
cards.notes: Locate the YMCA on the lower level through the mall directory, then confirm access or program requirements directly with the facility.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level YMCA listing within the Stonestown complex.
cards.evidence_claim: The Stonestown Galleria directory lists YMCA on the lower level near City Sports.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented SF State rituals and recurring campus traditions, from the entering-class pinning to student-made film showcases.

cards.title: GatorFest!
cards.subtitle: Fall welcome tradition for new Gators
cards.notes: Check the current GatorFest schedule before fall term begins, then choose a welcome event, activity or campus introduction that fits your first week.
cards.short_summary: SF State’s annual, multi-event welcome celebration starts the academic year.
cards.evidence_claim: SF State says it hosts GatorFest! annually to welcome new Gators through events that introduce students to peers, campus and the city.
cards.source_title: GatorFest! 2024 welcomes students to campus and the city
cards.access_notes: Dates, locations and participation details vary by year; consult the current GatorFest schedule.

cards.title: Get pinned with your entering class
cards.subtitle: GatorFest! · Cox Stadium
cards.notes: If you are an entering student, look for the pinning ceremony during GatorFest and arrive in time to join your cohort’s campus welcome ritual.
cards.short_summary: New students are formally welcomed through an entering-year pinning ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: SF State’s GatorFest programming includes an entering-year pinning ceremony at Cox Stadium.
cards.source_title: GatorFest! kicks off new academic year with dozens of campus events
cards.access_notes: Scheduled as part of fall GatorFest programming; verify the current year’s time and eligibility.

cards.title: Find yourself in the entering-class photo
cards.subtitle: GatorFest! · Cox Stadium and Athletic Field
cards.notes: Bring your new classmates to the designated GatorFest gathering point and join the class photo when the entering-year ceremony is scheduled.
cards.short_summary: The entering cohort is photographed together during the fall welcome program.
cards.evidence_claim: SF State lists a class photo alongside its entering-year pinning ceremony in GatorFest programming.
cards.source_title: GatorFest! 2024 welcomes students to campus and the city
cards.access_notes: This is a fall GatorFest activity; confirm the current schedule and meeting location.

cards.title: Rec the Night
cards.subtitle: GatorFest! · Mashouf Wellness Center
cards.notes: Go during fall GatorFest to sample Campus Recreation activities and learn how to use the Mashouf Wellness Center alongside other new and returning students.
cards.short_summary: A fall-night introduction to SF State Campus Recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: Campus Recreation says Rec the Night occurs at the start of every fall semester as part of SF State’s GatorFest.
cards.source_title: Campus Recreation Special Events
cards.access_notes: Held at the start of fall semester; event offerings and entry details are announced with the current GatorFest schedule.

cards.title: Costume Dodgeball
cards.subtitle: October tradition · Mashouf Wellness Center
cards.notes: Form a team of 10, follow Campus Recreation’s current registration rules and wear a safe Halloween costume for this seasonal dodgeball tournament.
cards.short_summary: Teams play dodgeball in costume during SF State’s October programming.
cards.evidence_claim: SF State Campus Recreation calls its Costume Dodgeball Tournament its favorite spooky-season tradition and describes teams of 10 competing in costumes.
cards.source_title: Campus Recreation Special Events
cards.access_notes: Occurs in October; registration, equipment and costume-safety rules should be checked with Campus Recreation.

cards.title: Walk, run or roll the annual 5K
cards.subtitle: Spring tradition · Malcolm X Plaza
cards.notes: Watch for spring registration, then take part at your own pace in the accessible 5K route that begins and ends at Malcolm X Plaza.
cards.short_summary: A spring campus 5K designed for walking, running or rolling.
cards.evidence_claim: Campus Recreation identifies the 5K Walk, Run and Roll as SF State’s annual 5K and says it begins and ends at Malcolm X Plaza.
cards.source_title: Campus Recreation Special Events
cards.access_notes: Held in spring; check the current Campus Recreation listing for registration, route and accessibility information.

cards.title: Earth Week, Gator-style
cards.subtitle: Campuswide April celebration
cards.notes: Use the annual Earth Week lineup to join a climate-focused activity, such as a campus fair, craft event or outdoor program, based on current offerings.
cards.short_summary: A campuswide annual celebration built around climate action and community.
cards.evidence_claim: SF State News says Earth Week, centralized campuswide in 2023, has become one of the University’s annual traditions.
cards.source_title: SFSU celebrates Earth Week with action, optimism and fun
cards.access_notes: Program dates and activities change each April; use the current University calendar or Earth Week listing.

cards.title: Film Finals
cards.subtitle: School of Cinema student-film showcase
cards.notes: Follow the School of Cinema and University calendar near semester’s end to catch the juried screening of selected SF State student films.
cards.short_summary: A juried showcase of SF State student films with more than a half-century of history.
cards.evidence_claim: SF State describes Film Finals as a Gator tradition for more than half a century and a juried showcase of the year’s student films.
cards.source_title: May 8, 2023 CampusMemo
cards.access_notes: Screening dates and venues vary; verify the current School of Cinema or University Calendar event listing.

cards.title: BECAfest
cards.subtitle: Broadcast and Electronic Communication Arts showcase
cards.notes: Check the BECA and University calendar near the end of the academic year to attend the annual showcase of student media work.
cards.short_summary: An annual celebration of SF State BECA students’ video, audio, writing and radio work.
cards.evidence_claim: SF State identifies BECAfest as the annual showcase and celebration of work produced by Broadcast and Electronic Communication Arts students.
cards.source_title: May 8, 2023 CampusMemo
cards.access_notes: Event date, venue and attendance details vary by year; consult current BECA or University Calendar announcements.

cards.title: The 12 academic hoods at Commencement
cards.subtitle: SF State Commencement tradition
cards.notes: At Commencement, watch for the undergraduate and graduate representatives selected by each academic college to wear their college’s academic hood.
cards.short_summary: Each college selects two graduating representatives for a visible Commencement honor.
cards.evidence_claim: SF State describes the selection of one undergraduate and one graduate from each academic college to wear the college hood at Commencement as a longstanding tradition.
cards.source_title: College of Health & Social Sciences student news
cards.access_notes: This is part of the formal Commencement ceremony; ceremony attendance and viewing information is published for each graduating class.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at San Francisco State University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure first-weekend sequence for getting oriented, finding campus resources, and sampling student-facing spaces.

cards.title: Start by locating the essentials
cards.subtitle: Campus map and directory
cards.notes: Open the official map before setting out, then mark the Library, Student Center, wellness center, dining halls, and event spaces you want to revisit.
cards.short_summary: Turn a large campus into a short, practical walking route.
cards.evidence_claim: SF State’s official campus map provides a directory of main-campus destinations and map locations.
cards.source_title: Welcome | Campus Maps
cards.access_notes: Use the online map and directory to confirm locations and accessibility details before going.

cards.title: Make the Library your first indoor landmark
cards.subtitle: 1630 Holloway Avenue
cards.notes: Walk through the main Library, note the study-room and help-desk locations, and save its spaces page for later when you need a quieter reset.
cards.short_summary: A central place to orient yourself to study support and campus services.
cards.evidence_claim: The Library provides study rooms, help desks, computers, printing, quiet-study areas, and other student-facing spaces.
cards.source_title: Spaces | J. Paul Leonard Library
cards.access_notes: Check the Library’s current hours and room-reservation information before planning a visit.

cards.title: See what is on view in Special Collections
cards.subtitle: J. Paul Leonard Library, fourth floor
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition, then head to the fourth floor for a short visual break that connects campus study spaces with archival material.
cards.short_summary: A free gallery stop beside Special Collections & Archives.
cards.evidence_claim: The Special Collections Gallery presents Library Special Collections and Archives exhibitions and is free and open to the campus community and general public.
cards.source_title: Spaces | J. Paul Leonard Library
cards.access_notes: The Gallery is on the fourth floor; exhibition availability and hours should be checked before visiting.

cards.title: Find the State Library branch upstairs
cards.subtitle: J. Paul Leonard Library, fifth and sixth floors
cards.notes: Add Sutro Library to your mental map of the building and look for its public research resources when you want to explore rare books or local history.
cards.short_summary: A California State Library branch within the SF State Library building.
cards.evidence_claim: The fifth and sixth floors of the J. Paul Leonard Library house Sutro Library, part of the California State Library.
cards.source_title: Information for Students | J. Paul Leonard Library
cards.access_notes: Review Sutro Library access details and current hours before a research visit.

cards.title: Use the Student Center as your meetup point
cards.subtitle: 1650 Holloway Avenue
cards.notes: Walk through the Student Center and choose a recognizable meeting spot; it contains restaurants, meeting spaces, Jack Adams Hall, and Malcolm X Plaza.
cards.short_summary: A practical hub for food, meetings, and campus programming.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Center houses restaurants and meeting spaces, including Jack Adams Hall and Malcolm X Plaza, and is operated by Associated Students.
cards.source_title: Event Centers | Conference & Event Services
cards.access_notes: Individual businesses, offices, and events in the building have separate access and operating schedules.

cards.title: Pick up the day’s campus details
cards.subtitle: Cesar Chavez Student Center, Plaza Level
cards.notes: Stop at the Information Center for a campus map, daily event schedule, general information, and details about scheduled campus tours before making later plans.
cards.short_summary: A first-weekend information checkpoint inside the Student Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Associated Students Information Center offers campus maps, daily event schedules, general information, event promotion, and scheduled campus-tour information.
cards.source_title: Information Center | Associated Students
cards.access_notes: Located on the Plaza Level of the Student Center; verify current operating hours online.

cards.title: Take a no-cost game break
cards.subtitle: Cesar Chavez Student Center, Recreation and Dining Level
cards.notes: Bring a classmate or roommate for a casual pool, console, or board-game break, and use the space to decompress between your campus walk and evening plans.
cards.short_summary: A free Student Center recreation space with pool, consoles, and games.
cards.evidence_claim: Rack-N-Cue is a free recreational space for SF State students, staff, and alumni, with pool tables, video game consoles, and board games.
cards.source_title: Rack-n-Cue | Associated Students
cards.access_notes: The page lists academic-semester hours of Monday through Friday, 10:30 a.m.–7:30 p.m.; confirm changes before visiting.

cards.title: Check whether an exhibition is open
cards.subtitle: Fine Arts Building, Room 238
cards.notes: Look at the gallery’s exhibition calendar before walking over, then use the visit as a focused stop rather than assuming a show is currently installed.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus gallery with exhibitions scheduled during open periods.
cards.evidence_claim: Fine Arts Gallery is in the Fine Arts Building, Room 238, and is open during exhibitions; its regular gallery hours are Tuesday through Friday, noon to 4 p.m.
cards.source_title: Visit | Fine Arts Gallery
cards.access_notes: Open only during exhibitions; consult the exhibition events calendar and current gallery hours before going.

cards.title: Locate your recreation and wellness hub
cards.subtitle: 755 Font Boulevard
cards.notes: Walk to the Mashouf Wellness Center, check current facility information, and decide whether a future workout, group-fitness class, court reservation, or swim fits your routine.
cards.short_summary: Campus Recreation’s main facility for fitness, recreation, and wellness.
cards.evidence_claim: Campus Recreation welcomes the SF State community to the Mashouf Wellness Center at 755 Font Boulevard and publishes facility and group-fitness information.
cards.source_title: Campus Recreation | San Francisco State University
cards.access_notes: Access and programming may require eligibility, membership, registration, or reservations; check the Member Portal and current facility hours.

cards.title: End by checking an all-ages evening listing
cards.subtitle: Cesar Chavez Student Center, Lower Conference Level
cards.notes: Review The Depot’s calendar for an open mic, music set, art social, or comedy night, and confirm the individual event details before heading back to campus.
cards.short_summary: An all-ages campus venue for music and other arts programming.
cards.evidence_claim: The Depot hosts live music, open mics, art socials, comedy nights, and more; its events are all ages and free and open to the public unless otherwise noted.
cards.source_title: The Depot | Associated Students
cards.access_notes: Most events take place Monday through Thursday between 6 and 9 p.m.; confirm the current event listing because exceptions may apply.
